trials.rationale: Measured facts: original clean step_ms is 112.02/111.98 ms per rank (max-rank 112.02; <=1.05x ceiling ~117.6 ms). The single observed invocation (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb) contains every phase (4x microbatch_forward_backward, optimizer_step, train_step, run). Per rank it moves exactly 497,759,232 B of fp32 gradients through 13 real NCCL allreduces (calls d0938de87369efd500322679 x12 at 28,351,488 B and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b x1 at 157,541,376 B = 124,439,808 params x 4 B). The transport is P2P-less and NVLink-less (peer_access 0/0, NVML status 3); NCCL tuning logs show RING SIMPLE with only channels {0..1}, and the separately calibrated clean completion medians are 1.99 ms per 28 MB bucket and 10.48 ms for the 157 MB bucket, i.e. ~34.4 ms of transport-bound communication per step at ~14.5 GB/s logical. Per-rank GPU compute in the step is ~27.5 ms for the 4 microbatch fwd/bwd (GPT2LMHeadModel family, 27,477 us / 4 invocations) plus ~2-3 ms of optimizer kernels. That accounts for ~60-65 ms of GPU-busy work against a 112 ms clean step: ~45-50 ms per step is consumed by no kernel at all - eager CPU dispatch and inter-rank skew across ~4,000 kernel launches per step (nsys: 3999 CUDA kernels; execution_timeline shows 6.4-7.4 ms CPU-submit spread per collective under perturbed collection, illustrating how skew inflates NCCL wait). Gradient volume and fp32 numerics are frozen, so leaf-group or joint candidates cannot attack either dominant term: the 34.4 ms is transport-bound on a fixed byte count, the ~45-50 ms overhead spans the entire eager loop (microbatch modules, optimizer_step add_/mul.out groups, and the run-phase allreduce/grad-accumulation calls together), and the baseline DDP bucket args, no_sync split and foreach=False SGD are explicitly listed as non-frozen implementation choices. The one coherent editable boundary that can legally restructure execution of the whole accumulated step - loop, synchronization pattern, gradient zeroing and update, all inside the timed run() - is the whole-workload project boundary, explicitly replacing the whole bundle per the binding contract. All 3,877 observed calls execute inside this boundary and their dispatch is affected by the plan, so affected_calls lists every observed call ID.
trials.hypothesis: Primary (to be tested): replacing the whole timed step at the project.invoke boundary with an execution policy that (a) runs the eager accumulated step during warmup to materialize static gradient buffers, then captures the complete step - the 4 microbatch forward/backwards, gradient flattening plus a real allreduce(SUM)/world_size on the default NCCL group (replacing the DDP reducer, which is a non-frozen baseline choice), in-graph gradient zeroing, and in-place p.add_(g, alpha=-lr) updates - into a CUDA graph, and (b) replays it for every measured invocation, will eliminate most of the ~45-50 ms dispatch/skew term. Because inputs are fixed per rank, reset() reloads state in place, dropout is 0 and attention is eager, replay executes the identical eager kernels on identical addresses, so numerics should be bitwise-equal to the captured eager step, cross-rank gradients stay bit-identical (identical post-allreduce buffers, atol=0 check), and the separately profiled communication diagnostic still observes the same device NCCL kernels. Expected landing zone is the GPU-bound floor of roughly 60-70 ms max-rank step_ms, far inside the 1.05x constraint; the benefit is a hypothesis to be measured, not a prediction of acceptance. Secondary, independently testable within the same boundary: raising the NCCL channel count above the observed 2 for the P2P-less PCIe path before first communicator use could reduce the ~34.4 ms transport-bound term (14.4 GB/s measured vs PCIe headroom). Known risks and fallbacks: capture of the default-group NCCL allreduce and the autograd engine on torch 2.13.0+cu129 / NCCL 2.29.7 is unverified on this worker; if whole-step capture fails, capture only the fwd/bwd compute and keep communication eager, which still removes most dispatch gaps. Grad zeroing moves from zero_grad(set_to_none=True) to an in-graph .zero_() inside the timed region (set_to_none is not representable statically); zeroing stays inside the timed step as required but the letter of the flag differs and must be defended. Reference-gradient equality after replacing the DDP reducer with flat SUM/2 accumulation must be measured (expected within fp32 reordering, tolerance grad_atol=1e-6/grad_rtol=1e-4). Whole-bundle replacement means per-group inherited call coverage is subsumed at the project boundary; runtime traces must corroborate that the captured kernels execute every invocation, since graph replay does not rerun Python hooks.

trials.rationale: Repair of the rejected trial-0ee027f2e6 whole-step execution plan; the boundary stays the one coherent whole-bundle replacement at project.invoke (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0), inside which every one of the 3877 observed calls executes, so affected_calls lists all of them. Measured facts: original clean step_ms is 112.02/111.98 ms (max-rank 112.02, <=1.05x ceiling 117.62 ms, project.json original_baseline). Per step each rank moves exactly 497,759,232 B of fp32 gradients through 13 real NCCL allreduces (calls d0938de87369efd500322679 x12 at 28,351,488 B and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b x1 at 157,541,376 B; collective_calibration-1af5837f medians 1.99 ms and 10.48 ms -> ~34.4 ms transport at ~14.3-15.0 GB/s logical on both sizes, i.e. bandwidth-bound at fixed frozen byte count; nccl_tuning-f6198e01 shows RING SIMPLE on channels {0..1} only on a P2P-less/NVLink-less path). nsys-9ed9145c counts 3999 CUDA kernels per step; fwd/bwd module time is ~27.5 ms (GPT2LMHeadModel family 27,477 us over 4 invocations) plus ~2-3 ms optimizer kernels, so ~45-50 ms of the 112 ms wall is CPU dispatch gaps and inter-rank skew, not any kernel. execution_timeline-1221e205 measures 6.4-7.4 ms per-collective CPU-submit spread between ranks under perturbed collection, and the profiled diagnostic nccl kernel sum is 220.08 ms on rank 0 vs 34.79 ms on rank 1: waiting/skew, not transport, dominates that diagnostic (profiled wall 1482/1500 ms is perturbed and is not project J; binding_cost parent/passthrough medians 117.6/114.2 vs 106.8/123.2 ms are likewise collector-noisy and not acceptance evidence). Why this failure happened and is now repairable: the previous trial was rejected as no_valid_parameter_candidate - all 3 parameter endpoints (nccl_channels 2/4/8) failed validity at 119.29/123.56/125.40 ms, above the 117.62 ms ceiling. candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6 shows the concrete cause: both CUDA-graph capture attempts aborted with RuntimeError 'Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned' raised at transformers 5.16.1 masking_utils.py:603 eager_mask via modeling_gpt2.py:583 create_causal_mask - torch.tensor(0.0, device=cuda) performs a pageable H2D copy that is illegal under capture. The ladder then ran its eager composite, which is slower than baseline for a now-understood reason: it replaces DDP's overlap of bucket allreduces with the last backward by a strictly post-backward flat allreduce over the same 497,759,232 B (~33 ms at the measured rate - the calibration shows consolidating into one collective does NOT cut transport) and adds ~300 no-op copy kernels and 1 GB of self-copies because p.grad already aliases the flat buffer. So the fallback design, not the boundary, produced the invalid endpoints. Concrete repairs verified against the installed transformers 5.16.1 source: (1) masking_utils._preprocess_mask_arguments returns an already-4D attention_mask as-is (masking_utils.py:810-812), and GPT2Model.forward passes it through to the eager path where attn_weights = attn_weights + mask (modeling_gpt2.py:583, 60-61); precomputing the (1,1,128,128) fp32 causal mask once outside capture with bitwise-identical values (torch.where(tril, 0.0, torch.finfo(torch.float32).min)) and passing it as attention_mask removes the capture-unsafe H2D copy from every microbatch forward while keeping bitwise-identical numerics (the loss path - nn.functional.pad/cross_entropy - has no other CPU-tensor H2D). (2) The failure ladder must end at the installed parent callable (context.references['5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0'], measured ~112 ms <= ceiling) instead of the no-overlap flat composite; any capture failure then still yields a valid endpoint. (3) Keep the flat allreduce(SUM)/world_size as one real NCCL collective inside the captured step - per element it is the same single fp32 cross-rank add plus exact /2 the DDP bucketed reducer performs, so synchronized gradients stay bit-identical across ranks and match the serial reference (baseline parent checks measured max_abs_error 0.0) - and drop the self-copy loops. DDP construction args, the no_sync split, foreach=False SGD and zero_grad(set_to_none=True) are documented non-frozen implementation choices; zeroing moves to an in-graph flat.zero_() that stays inside the timed step, satisfying the no-pre-clearing invariant. Group/joint scopes cannot attack either dominant term: gradient bytes, fp32 numerics and per-op kernels are frozen, the 34.4 ms transport is bandwidth-bound at fixed bytes regardless of bucket layout, and the ~45-50 ms dispatch/skew spans the entire eager loop across all phases, so only whole-step execution restructuring at the project boundary can remove it.
trials.hypothesis: Primary (to be tested): with the transformers mask H2D eliminated, the warmup capture of the complete step (flat zeroing, 4 microbatch forward/backwards with precomputed 4D causal masks, one flat NCCL allreduce(SUM)/2, in-place p.add_ updates) succeeds on torch 2.13.0+cu129 / NCCL 2.29.7 and replay per measured invocation collapses ~3999 kernel launches to one graph launch plus one allreduce, removing most of the ~45-50 ms dispatch/skew term. Expected landing zone is GPU-busy plus the flat allreduce, roughly 60-70 ms max-rank step_ms, far inside the 117.62 ms ceiling; the benefit is a hypothesis to measure, not a prediction. Numerics should be bitwise-equal to the eager step: identical kernels on identical addresses (dropout 0, eager attention, fixed per-rank inputs, reset() reloads state in place so replay works across repeats and continuous steps), exact cross-rank equality from identical post-allreduce bytes, and grad/param comparisons expected at the 0.0 max_abs_error the baseline achieves because SUM then exact /2 is the same per-element arithmetic DDP performs. Known risks and fallbacks: NCCL-collective capture on this exact stack is unverified (the previous attempt aborted at the mask op before reaching NCCL), so keep the consensus ladder - if any capture level fails, delegate to the installed parent step (valid ~112 ms) rather than the removed flat eager composite; graph replay does not rerun Python hooks, so quality coverage relies on the replaced whole bundle at the project boundary and runtime traces must corroborate the replayed kernels every invocation. Secondary, independently testable in the same boundary: raising NCCL channel count above the observed 2 for the P2P-less ring before the communicator's first use could cut the ~33 ms flat allreduce; the previous 3-trial failure at every nccl_channels value was plan-level slowness of the eager fallback, not evidence about channels, so this axis stays an open hypothesis. The separately profiled communication_kernel_sum_ms diagnostic keeps seeing the step's own single NCCL allreduce per invocation and stays a diagnostic, not the score.

trials.rationale: Repair of rejected trial-592873c70d at the same single coherent whole-bundle boundary: project.invoke (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0), inside which all 3877 observed calls execute, so affected_calls lists every one of them. Measured facts: original clean step_ms is 112.02/111.98 ms max-rank (ceiling 117.62 ms, project.json); the accepted parent itself measured 114.12/101.29 ms in the rejecting AB/BA. Why the previous candidate failed (feedback evidence, not hypothesis): its CUDA-graph ladder never engaged in measurement - coverage shows routes eager_boot_step (1) + parent_fallback_capture_failed (1) - so the timed path was the slower no-overlap flat-eager composite plus the parent step, with NCCL_NCHANNELS=4 set at build, a second dedicated NCCL communicator and a ~475 MiB flat gradient buffer retained (peak_allocated 2477 MB vs 1977 MB baseline); candidate medians 116.05/119.05 ms beat neither the ceiling (117.62) nor the paired noise bounds (6.50/1.76 ms, paired gains -1.9/-17.8 ms). The nccl_channels axis is dead evidence: screening endpoints 112.63/114.38/114.77 ms at 2/4/8 channels are all at-or-above baseline, and nccl_tuning-f6198e01 shows RING SIMPLE on channels {0..1} moving the frozen 497,759,232 B per step at ~14-15 GB/s (collective_calibration-1af5837f medians 1.99 ms per 28,351,488 B bucket, 10.48 ms per 157,541,376 B bucket), i.e. transport is bandwidth-bound at fixed bytes; channel or bucket-layout edits cannot cut it. Where the recoverable time actually is (current discovery, same revision): 3999 CUDA kernels per step per rank (nsys-9ed9145c); non-NCCL kernel busy is only ~35.5 ms (rank 0) / ~40.8 ms (rank 1), of which ~21 ms is GEMM and ~12-15 ms is 2048 elementwise launches; the perturbed NCCL diagnostic sum (220.08 ms rank 0 vs 34.79 ms rank 1) plus execution_timeline-1221e205's 6.4-7.4 ms per-collective CPU-submit spread show rank-0 dispatch lag, not transport, dominates waiting. The adapter executes the four per-rank microbatches as four separate (1,128) forward/backwards: four full eager module dispatch trees (~608 nn.Module calls, ~1000 kernel launches each) and four weight-streaming passes whose GEMMs are weight-read bound at M=128, so the dominant weight traffic is paid four times. That loop lives in the frozen adapter's _accumulate/run; no module, group or joint replacement can merge four loss.backward() calls across invocations, and no operator-scope edit changes the loop or the shapes - only the whole-bundle replacement at project.invoke can. The repair keeps everything that worked and removes everything that failed: plain eager batched execution of the same workload - torch.cat of the rank's own current 4 microbatches (per-rank sharding preserved), one DDP-wrapped forward (same DDP: broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True), per-microbatch CE losses computed from the batched logits and stacked-summed with each divided by accumulation_steps=4 exactly as gpt2_ddp_training.py:36-45 defines, one backward that triggers the same 13 bucketed allreduces (12x28,351,488 B + 1x157,541,376 B, membership per communication-ownership.json) overlapped with backward exactly as the baseline 4th-microbatch backward does, then the unchanged foreach=False SGD optimizer.step() and torch.cuda.synchronize(); zero_grad(set_to_none=True) stays inside the timed step. No CUDA graph capture (nothing to fail), no NCCL env parameters, no second communicator, no flat buffer; a runtime failure delegates to the installed parent step (a valid ~108-114 ms endpoint under the ceiling), never to a slower composite.
trials.hypothesis: Primary (to be tested): executing the four per-rank microbatches as one batched (4,128) forward/backward leaves the gradient math per element identical - local grad = d(sum_i loss_i/4)/dw, DDP bucket allreduce SUM then exact /2 is the same single fp32 cross-rank add per element the baseline performs, so exact cross-rank equality (atol=0) holds and the serial global-batch comparison stays within grad/param tolerances 1e-6/1e-4; the only numerical deviation is GEMM/tile rounding from M=512 instead of M=128 (~1e-7 relative, ~3 orders of magnitude of margin; the previous candidate measured max_abs_error 0.0 with equally-shaped fp32 arithmetic). Expected benefit: GPU GEMM time drops toward a single weight-streaming pass (~15 ms of the ~21 ms), ~1500 of the 2048 elementwise launches and ~1800 Python module dispatches disappear, cutting a large share of the ~40 ms dispatch/skew term and the per-collective submit spread; transport stays ~34 ms unchanged. Landing zone roughly 70-95 ms max-rank step_ms vs 112.02 baseline - far inside the 117.62 ms ceiling and well beyond the 6.50/1.76 ms paired noise bounds; treat all of this as hypothesis, not prediction. Risks and tests: batched-vs-serial reference gradient deltas must stay under tolerance (observe() reports max_abs_error; abort to parent if not), peak_allocated_bytes rises ~100-150 MB from batched logits/activations (context only, not a constraint), and the separately profiled communication_kernel_sum_ms diagnostic keeps seeing the step's own 13 NCCL bucket kernels and stays a diagnostic. The workload executes on current inputs every invocation (re-cat each call), reset() semantics are untouched, and coverage rests on the replaced whole bundle at the project boundary corroborated by runtime kernel traces, since no Python hooks inside the bundle are skipped by this eager design.

invariants: Workload dimensions and amounts are read from request['workload'] (id 'accumulated_step': world_size=2, micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4) and the launched world size must equal workload world_size (gpt2_ddp_training.py:56-57; the frozen adapter raises otherwise in prepare(), adapter.py:130-137); the workload row is copied verbatim from workloads.json gpt2_ddp_training.workloads[0] (the entry always uses workloads[0] and ignores held_out_workloads), so effective_batch = world_size*micro_batch*accumulation_steps = 8 and tokens_per_step = world_size*micro_batch*sequence_length*accumulation_steps = 1024 are frozen by the request.

Per-rank input sharding is required workload semantics (request notes; gpt2_ddp_training.py:30-33): each rank processes only its own accumulation_steps=4 microbatches, torch.randint(0, 50257, (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128)) from a torch.Generator seeded 31000+rank; the serial reference consumes all ranks' shards in rank order (adapter.py:104-110 builds them per rank and adapter.py:157, 254-258 keeps and uses CPU copies of all ranks' shards).

Deterministic seeding for reference reproducibility (gpt2_ddp_training.py:24-27; adapter.py:42-43, 91-101): weights from torch.manual_seed(20261020) immediately before model construction using the workloads.json gpt2_ddp_training.model spec (n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024); per-rank input generator seeds 31000+rank; these seeds must not change.

Numerical policy is frozen by the request/source (common.py:34-42 configure, gpt2_ddp_training.py:26-27; adapter.py:61-73, 93-101): FP32 everywhere (.float()), torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, float32_matmul_precision='highest', cudnn.benchmark=False, eager attention, all dropout 0, use_cache=False; submissions must not change these policies or loosen accuracy.

Loss and gradient semantics (gpt2_ddp_training.py:36-45; adapter.py:113-122, 236-268): each of the 4 per-rank microbatch CE losses is divided by accumulation_steps=4 before backward, with the divided losses stacked and summed per rank; the synchronized DDP gradients must equal the serial global-batch reference (all world_size*accumulation_steps = 8 microbatches in rank order, each loss divided by that global count of 8) within grad_atol=1e-06, grad_rtol=1e-04 from request['quality'].

The step's required work includes the gradient collectives themselves: real NCCL synchronization on the backend 'nccl' default process group with world_size 2 must happen inside the timed run() (request 'Required work includes the gradient collectives themselves'; adapter.py:208-216); the baseline pattern is model.no_sync() on the first 3 of 4 microbatches with the last microbatch's backward triggering the DDP all-reduce (gpt2_ddp_training.py:40; adapter.py:117).

Primary goal and metric scope, updated by this request: minimize clean step_ms for the same complete accumulated training step. step_ms is the wall time of the timed step (the framework's timing of run(), adapter.py:208-216) between CUDA synchronizations, excluding reset, the gloo control-group barrier and CUDA sync at measurement boundaries (adapter.py:201-205), all observe()/correctness work, profiling and report writing. Per aligned repeat the maximum across the 2 ranks is taken - rank times are never summed or averaged - and then the median over repeats is reported (rank_aggregation 'max', aggregation_order 'ranks_then_samples'; the source's own combination does exactly this at gpt2_ddp_training.py:149-151 with the median from common.py:66-71, and metrics() reports the per-invocation step_ms unchanged, adapter.py:364-388).

Goal constraint retained from request['objective']['constraints'] and workloads.json step_ms_max_baseline_ratio: the max-rank-then-median clean step_ms must remain <= 1.05x the same quantity measured on the original baseline. The baseline's implementation choices (DDP bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, broadcast_buffers=False; no_sync() on the first 3 of 4 microbatches; foreach=False SGD; gloo control group for barriers; default reducer during communication measurement) are not frozen requirements - semantics-equivalent alternatives are allowed subject to the quality checks and this step-time constraint.

Measurement policy is frozen by the request: measurement_lifetime 'invocation' (one measured invocation = one complete DDP-accumulated GPT-2 training step), warmup=2, repeats=5 clean samples with the median reported, continuous_steps=2, worker_timeout_s=900; the entry's own sampling discipline (at least one warmup and three clean samples, common.py:28-29) stays satisfied. peak_allocated_bytes is still collected per repeat (per-process CUDA allocated peak, max across ranks) but is reported context only, not part of this request's objective or constraints.

Completion boundary is unchanged: after the step's torch.cuda.synchronize() every rank's full gradients are bit-identical across ranks and match, within workloads.json grad tolerances, the serial single-GPU reference that processes the identical 8-sample global batch from the same starting parameters; post-step parameters match the reference update within parameter tolerances; the accumulated loss is finite (request 'completion'; adapter.py:294-361 raises on any violation).

Exact cross-rank gradient equality is asserted with atol=0.0, rtol=0.0 via rank-0 broadcast on the default group for every parameter (gpt2_ddp_training.py:81-86; adapter.py:219-233); it runs in observe() outside all timing and raises on violation.

The timed step comprises zero_grad(set_to_none=True), all accumulation_steps=4 forward/backward microbatches with the synchronization split, optimizer.step() and torch.cuda.synchronize() (gpt2_ddp_training.py:102-105; adapter.py:113-122, 208-216); gradients must not be pre-cleared outside the timed region - the source's zero_grad stays inside the timed accumulation (adapter.py:114).

Post-step parameters must match the serial reference update within parameter_atol=1e-06, parameter_rtol=1e-04 with the source's SGD update rule lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0 (gpt2_ddp_training.py:60, 88-91; adapter.py:154-156, 337-341).
The +1-corruption negative control must be rejected by the gradient tolerance check (common.py:79-84 negative_check; adapter.py:286-291, 351-353); it is re-verified in observe() outside timing.

Full required observations are preserved: accumulated loss, every parameter gradient and every updated parameter as detached CPU tensors, plus finite-loss and check outcomes; no performance counters or elapsed times enter observations (adapter.py:294-361) - step_ms comes only from the framework's timing of run(), surfaced unchanged through metrics() (adapter.py:364-388).

communication_kernel_sum_ms is retained as a separate required diagnostic observation (request['required_observations'] and workload goal id 'communication', metric diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms with constraint step_ms_max_baseline_ratio=1.05), not the primary score and not wire time: per-rank sum of device NCCL kernel durations from exactly 3 separately profiled invocations (range(3), source-fixed) of the same step, maximum across ranks per aligned invocation, then the median of the 3 values (workloads.json communication_metric_caveat; gpt2_ddp_training.py:122-125, 156-157; common.py:87-105); it is mapped to the framework-collected torch_communication.communication_kernel_sum_ms, runs separately from the 5 clean-timing repeats, and collector availability must be verified by the actual workload worker per deployment.json (request notes).

The clean timing path (measure/profile modes) must stay free of extra collectives so the communication collector sees only the step's own communication (adapter.py runs no additional collectives around the timed step, adapter.py:201-216); the separate bucket-inventory comm-hook run stays outside all measurements and does not alter the reducer used for clean timing (gpt2_ddp_training.py:126-138).

State protocol is frozen: reset() restores the exact initial state before each measured step - reload of the initial CPU state_dict, optimizer-state clear, CPU/CUDA RNG snapshot restore, run counter and reference anchor zeroed - without destroying the process group (gpt2_ddp_training.py:99-100; adapter.py:187-194); repeated invocations from reset must reproduce the observations used as per-rank references, and for framework continuous step k>1 the rank-0 serial reference is anchored to the observed post-step-(k-1) full state_dict snapshot (the exact parameter point the distributed run started that step from), using full state_dict snapshots because named_parameters() deduplicates GPT-2's tied lm_head/wte weight (adapter.py:236-283, 326-329, 354 and its repair note, adapter.py:11-23).

The evaluator is frozen and executes unchanged: adapter.py already supports this contract - prepare() validates the declared world size and applies the numerical/seeding policy (adapter.py:125-184), run() executes the complete accumulated step including the NCCL gradient synchronization between the framework's CUDA synchronizations (adapter.py:208-216), observe() enforces every correctness check outside timing (adapter.py:294-361), and metrics() reports step_ms, tokens_per_second from the unchanged work amount, tokens_per_step=1024, effective_batch=8 and the other retained quantities (adapter.py:364-388); submissions must satisfy these invariants within that frozen support and must not generate or edit adapter/evaluator code, loosen accuracy, or invent measurements.
